slides.title: Sleeping Machines
slides.subtitle: AI that learns what to compute, when to compute it, and what to remember.
slides.notes: Private review deck. The founder proposes a €3M raise. €50M priced pre-money is the central bullish negotiating thesis developed here; €100M is a stretch scenario, neither an independent fair-value appraisal nor an investor offer. The research evidence is exploratory and single-seed. No customer interest has been reported. No investor, vendor or customer has been contacted in preparing this deck.

slides.title: Model capacity and the cost of using it must scale differently.
slides.subtitle: The opportunity: preserve useful intelligence while reducing the work paid for each prediction.
slides.notes: This is the problem definition and investment hypothesis. It is not a claim that all existing architectures perform dense work or lack memory. MoE already separates available parameters from selected computation; recurrent and selective-state models already retain state. Our proposed contribution is a temporal race/state/alternative-credit construction and its tested consequences. Software and hardware benefits must be evaluated with tuned incumbents under the same workload boundaries.

cards.label: MODEL CAPACITY
cards.body: Larger models and richer memory can improve capability. Accessing that capacity still costs computation and data movement.

cards.label: DEPLOYMENT ECONOMICS
cards.body: Serving cost, latency and memory determine whether capability can be deployed in constrained environments.

cards.label: OUR APPROACH
cards.body: Learn which local computations to activate; retain local state and train the alternatives that were not selected.

slides.banner: We are developing a model family and execution substrate around this separation.

slides.title: Messages race. Selected memories update. Alternatives learn.
slides.subtitle: A simple event loop connects representation, timing and sparse computation.
slides.notes: This construction combines familiar vector operations with temporal computation and sparse state. Separate keys determine addressing; values determine delivered content. Counterfactual credit gives unrealized alternatives a learning signal without softening the hard forward route. The present implementation is not a physical asynchronous machine: autograd, shared training windows, clipping and Adam remain. Winner-only inference still scores all candidate keys.

steps.label: 01 / ENCODE
steps.body: A learned function produces a message and its arrival time from input and local memory.

steps.label: 02 / SELECT
steps.body: Arrival times select a receiver. Separate address keys and delivered values support sparse execution.

steps.label: 03 / REMEMBER
steps.body: Update the selected memory and propagate a new message into deeper computation.

steps.label: 04 / LEARN
steps.body: Use errors to improve message content and timing, including paths that were not selected.

slides.banner: Implemented language core: hard selection and persistent local state in a synchronous emulator.

slides.title: The language experiments establish three useful facts.
slides.subtitle: 10M-character text8 training budget; held-out prediction error. Lower bits per character is better.
slides.notes: T256 test values come from completed held-out evaluations; training scores and pending 90M results are excluded. One nominal pass uses about 9.994M training positions. A single seed and differing native/control training order limit generalization. The p96 improvement over LSTM is {best_lstm_gain:.4f} bpc, with {best_lstm_fit_ratio:.2f} times fitting work; it establishes a promising quality direction, not an iso-quality resource win.

cards.label: IT CAN LEARN REAL TEXT
cards.body: Best model reaches the saved recurrent baseline’s quality ({lstm_bpc:.3f}). It uses {best_lstm_fit_ratio:.2f}× estimated training work.

cards.label: ALTERNATIVE CREDIT HELPS
cards.body: In the same small model, learning from unchosen paths improves prediction error; estimated training work rises 0.30%.

cards.label: CAPACITY AND SELECTED WORK
cards.body: More available memory improves prediction while retaining eight selected writes per input. Key scoring and learning costs also grow.

slides.banner: Exploratory single-seed results. The next proof is replicated quality plus a measured system-cost advantage.

slides.title: A language-model foothold for a new architecture.
slides.subtitle: Held-out prediction error versus estimated training arithmetic; 10M characters, one pass.
slides.notes: p32 / D4 credited: {credit_bpc:.6f} bpc, 7.243 estimated whole-fit TFLOPs, 108,875 parameters. Saved Transformer-256×2: {transformer_bpc:.6f}, 111.262 TFLOPs, 1,658,907 parameters. This gives {transformer_fit_ratio:.2f}× lower fitting arithmetic and {transformer_parameter_ratio:.2f}× fewer parameters for this saved control, with {transformer_credit_gain:.4f} lower bpc. The strong one-pass LSTM is {lstm_bpc:.6f} at 20.306 TFLOPs. Best native p96 is {best_bpc:.6f} at 58.648 TFLOPs. A modern tuned Transformer/MoE/SSM and larger-data matched protocol are still needed.
slides.caveat: Saved one-pass controls; same test region and window length. Training order and work conventions differ. One seed. Arithmetic estimates are not service cost.

slides.title: Start with low-batch language inference on existing hardware.
slides.subtitle: Product hypothesis for local and on-premise text applications; no customer interest reported yet.
slides.notes: This is a product hypothesis chosen to make the research investable and testable, not a confirmed customer need. The present character-language fits do not establish a production-quality token model, application task performance or persistent cross-request serving. Low-batch inference is a proposed test venue for stateful sparse execution, not a measured region of advantage. Tune recurrent, modern Transformer/MoE and selective-state controls; include setup, memory, warmup, traffic, latency and energy. The ≥20% threshold is a proposed economic screen, not a forecast. No customer interest has been reported; demand interviews and evaluation partners remain future work.

cards.label: WHO WOULD EVALUATE IT
cards.body: Teams deploying small language models under latency, memory or cost constraints. Demand validation is a next step.

cards.label: WHAT WE WOULD SUPPLY
cards.body: A trained model, sparse inference runtime and a reproducible quality-and-cost evaluation on the intended workload.

cards.label: WHY THEY WOULD ADOPT
cards.body: Adoption depends on equivalent useful quality, service reliability and a measured reduction in complete deployment cost.

slides.banner: Commercial gate: target ≥20% full-system cost reduction at matched quality on one selected workload.

slides.title: Software establishes the advantage. Hardware can amplify it.
slides.subtitle: One research program, with staged routes to deployment.
slides.notes: The first commercial workload is a selection hypothesis rather than a confirmed customer request. A staged software route lowers dependency on new silicon and permits independent benchmarking. A clockless implementation could benefit from less global synchronization and local state, but clock precision, signal fanout, memory, interconnect and fabrication overhead may dominate. Hardware economic claims require measurements. Costs for an ASIC tapeout are not estimated or funded here.

cards.label: 01 / MODELS + RUNTIME
cards.body: Validate the language workload on existing hardware. License a model/runtime with auditable deployment economics.

cards.label: 02 / ACCELERATOR INTEGRATION
cards.body: Optimize supported hardware, compilers and memory access. Pursue joint evaluations and platform-specific licensing.

cards.label: 03 / EVENT-DRIVEN SILICON
cards.body: Translate learned timing and local state into hardware feasibility work. Expand to mobile, robotics and persistent agents.

cards.label: MODEL + LEARNING
cards.body: Timing, state and alternative-credit methods, supported by retained ablations and numerical contracts.

cards.label: RUNTIME + HARDWARE
cards.body: Sparse kernels, memory management, measurement and hardware mapping can reinforce the model advantage.

slides.title: Three gates determine whether this becomes a business.
slides.subtitle: Each gate has a falsifiable result and a consequence for further spending.
slides.notes: The principal investor risks are scalable prediction quality, economical execution and commercial adoption. Technical gaps include the trained float32 sparse-backend contract, longer memory/credit horizons, stable adaptation and hardware timing/precision. Corporate rights, team hiring and founder availability remain diligence items. The program preserves its architectural thesis while allowing a narrower viable product. No probability of success is assigned to these gates, and the €50M proposal is not inferred from benchmark scores.

cards.label: 01 / QUALITY AT SCALE
cards.body: Repeat across seeds and larger data with tuned controls. Small text8 results establish a foothold, not frontier capability.

cards.label: 02 / COMPLETE ECONOMICS
cards.body: Validate trained sparse execution, then charge traffic, latency, residency and energy. Arithmetic estimates alone do not establish savings.

cards.label: 03 / ADOPTION
cards.body: Identify a use case and an evaluator willing to test it. Confirm useful quality, integration effort and willingness to pay.

slides.banner: If a gate fails, diagnose or narrow the workload before committing more compute or new silicon.

slides.title: The next 18 months produce evidence investors can underwrite.
slides.subtitle: Proposed milestones measured from funding; spending advances with completed gates.
slides.notes: The timing is a planning assumption measured from funding. Three seeds and tuned modern controls are validation targets, not present assets. The ≥20% complete-cost gate is a proposed commercial screen and should be adapted to actual service requirements before experiments. Model quality and resource accounting must stay jointly comparable. Current owner queues retain priority; no new training or unguarded compute is launched to prepare this deck. Continued funding depends on completed results, measurable economics and a credible next workload rather than predictions entered as benchmark evidence.

stages.label: MONTHS 12–18

slides.title: The same model improves when unchosen paths receive credit.
slides.subtitle: Controlled small-model comparison; held-out error and estimated complete training work.
slides.notes: The local linearized credit estimator adds a derivative pathway for alternative delivered values while preserving the forward winner. It is not the exact full counterfactual trajectory gradient. The paired p32 / D4 T256 gain is {credit_gain:.6f} bpc, with {credit_fit_increase_pct:.4f}% extra whole-fit estimated operations. The corresponding p32 / D8 gain is {depth_credit_gain:.6f}. Attribution is stronger than a comparison between different widths, but a single seed still leaves variance and hyperparameter sensitivity unresolved.
stats: Timing-only credit versus added local alternative-value route credit.
Hard forward selection and parameter count retained.
Derived from the BPC difference; one controlled seed.
slides.detail: A deeper variant also improves by {depth_credit_gain:.3f} bits per character. Both are single-seed comparisons; numerical details and model definitions follow.
slides.banner: A falsifiable architectural mechanism, with a small counted arithmetic increment.

slides.title: More available state. The same eight selected writes.
slides.subtitle: Small model with alternative credit: available memory doubles; selected updates stay fixed.
slides.notes: Pool 2 → 4 changes memory scalars from 512 to 1,024 and parameters from 108,875 to 177,019. At T256, quality changes from {credit_bpc:.6f} to {pool_bpc:.6f}. Selected writes remain eight per input position; candidate keys increase 16 → 32. Winner-only per-position arithmetic increases {pool_sparse_increase_pct:.4f}%, but whole-fit estimated work rises {pool_fit_increase_pct:.4f}%. All memory and key scoring still cost resources. A negative uncredited pool expansion was measured at D8, while this positive credited pair is D4; this is not a full matched 2×2 interaction test.
slides.banner: Quality improves by {pool_gain:.3f} bpc; total capacity and learning costs remain explicitly charged.

slides.title: The sparse path is implemented; system proof is next.
slides.subtitle: Estimated arithmetic per evaluated input position. Green bars show the implemented winner-only path.
slides.notes: Small random float64 fixtures match full-emulator logits within roughly 1e-10. Actual trained float32 winner/state/cache parity and a full held-out rescore are prepared and pending. The prepared CPU worker retains prepacked matrices per fixed model version, but native admission remains unrun. Candidate key scans, copying, residency, setup, gather traffic, cache invalidation and quality must all be included in serving comparisons. The deck deliberately does not attach the trained quality to an unverified production backend or convert FLOPs to joules.
slides.caveat: These are backend/shape estimates. Native evaluation pays overlapping-window warmup (~2 positions/target); LSTM recurrent evaluation differs. Not a service-cost win.

slides.title: An adaptation signal exists. Its work is accounted for.
slides.subtitle: Predict-before-update experiment on a new text stream; separate from the latest model family.
slides.notes: Frozen versus online evaluation scores 8,191 targets with predict-before-update, 16-character delayed-feedback blocks, lr 1e-4, fresh Adam, clipping and full-backbone gradients. Both arms retain persistent local state. BPC improves by {online_gain:.6f}; total processing-operation estimates increase from 210,902,697 to 2,264,163,359, a {online_work_ratio:.4f}× ratio. This supports trainability under adaptation, not inexpensive lifelong learning. Retention, drift, long-horizon memory and local asynchronous learning need new evidence. Loihi 2 already provides an on-chip learning precedent.
slides.banner: Online-learning upside: persistent adaptive systems. Current result: one costed pilot.

slides.title: The contribution is the complete construction.
slides.subtitle: Established alternatives already address parts of this problem; they remain essential controls.
slides.notes: The pitch does not assert sole invention of sparse activation, gating, normalization, key/value separation or hardware learning. It proposes an integrated trainable temporal substrate and evaluates consequences. The latest native language model has no dense carrier or n-gram count component, but remains a restricted software realization. A weak result in one restricted variant should be diagnosed; genuine superiority requires matched strong controls. Intel Loihi 2 is cited on the adaptation and strategic slides.

Match quality/data and charge routing, memory traffic and training.
Persistent state and efficient sequence processing.
Test whether temporal races add useful quality or allocation.
Event-driven hardware and local learning precedents.
Prove expressive model quality, mapping and measured energy.
Joint timing, sparse memory, deep representation and alternative credit.
Scale integrated mechanisms without replacing them with dense carriers.

slides.title: AMD’s Silo AI deal supports the strategic logic.
slides.subtitle: Announced approximately $665M all-cash acquisition in 2024; a mature-company precedent.
slides.notes: AMD’s announcement connects the acquisition to end-to-end AI solutions, engineering expertise, enterprise customers and Poro/Viking model work using AMD platforms, including LUMI. It does not establish that chip usage alone caused the acquisition. Silo had a large team and existing customers; neither applies here. The approximately $665M announced transaction value and Liquid AI’s $250M Series A amount are different quantities and are not converted into our pre-money valuation. They demonstrate strategic precedent, not an offer, floor or near-term acquisition expectation.

Incumbents are also improving rapidly, which raises the threshold for a commercially useful alternative.

slides.title: Successful platform adoption can support very large outcomes.
slides.subtitle: Conditional commercial arithmetic illustrates the scale required; no forecast or market multiple claim.
slides.notes: The €10B/€50B equity scenarios use deliberately stated revenue multiples rather than observed comparables. They require economics, durable margins and value capture that are wholly unproven. Multiplying revenue by a selected multiple is not an enterprise/equity reconciliation: the examples assume negligible net debt at exit. The scenarios overlap and are alternatives, not additive. Infrastructure relevance can justify funding risky research, but cannot itself prove a current valuation. Smaller niche success, delayed commercialization, licensing-only outcomes, further dilution and total failure remain possible.
slides.detail: A cross-platform substrate could participate in cloud inference, persistent agents and embodied systems. Reaching these outcomes requires sustained quality, scale, margins and broad adoption.
slides.banner: The upside is large if the platform works and wins adoption. Its probability remains unmeasured.

slides.title: The completed comparisons, using consistent resource units.
slides.subtitle: Frozen 10M-character, one-pass evidence. Model definitions are on the next slide.
slides.notes: All fitting columns include estimated complete step arithmetic rather than forward-only model FLOPs. Native representative operator traces include backward, alternative credit, clipping and Adam; dense controls use shape formulas with backward approximately twice forward. Inference includes traced unit and special-function arithmetic, but not DRAM traffic, copying, allocation, RNG, evaluation overhead or physical energy. Formula conventions differ and are stated. Per-position columns use one shared denominator type per column. Winner-only arithmetic is explicitly separated from emulator quality. Full CSV contains all 13 native fits and both controls.
slides.caveat: Fit MF/pos = per training position. Inference MF/pos = per evaluated input position. Native quality uses training evaluator; winner-only trained parity/rescore pending. Native overlap warmup adds work per scored target. Full 15-row CSV retains older models.

slides.title: Plain-language labels map to reproducible model records.
slides.subtitle: Message width counts scalars; available memory counts local state slots.
slides.notes: These names are editorial labels for the frozen completed configurations, not new models, products or a production-version series. Each native configuration has two heads per layer. Selected writes per input position are eight at four layers and sixteen at eight layers. Available slots equal layers × heads × pool size. Credit means the local linearized alternative-value estimator. The small timing-only row and alternative-credit row share forward parameters and architecture. Full filenames, source/parent hashes, exact operation counts and seed/protocol fields are retained in the private evidence ledger.

slides.title: The comparison boundaries are part of the evidence.
slides.subtitle: Maintain the original records and disclose what a result actually measures.
slides.notes: The native score pays overlap-window warmup, evaluating roughly twice as many input positions as scored targets at T256. LSTM recurrent evaluation is a different protocol. Native T256 coverage is 999,936 targets, while original saved controls have a slightly different tail. The raw difference is small but must be disclosed. The 90M owner campaign is active; checkpoints count presented targets, including repeated random segments, and do not establish a final 90M held-out result. slides.title: Reverse-underwriting shows the assumptions behind a price.
slides.subtitle: This arithmetic is a sensitivity tool; the research does not estimate platform-success probabilities.
slides.notes: The illustrative model discounts the retained fraction of a successful future equity outcome to today and assigns zero failure value. It is not a complete corporate DCF, does not model all cash flows, and assumes the retained cohort benefits from an exit equity value after future financing. €10B exit × 30% retention / 1.15^10 is the conditional present value; €50M requires {required_probability_50_pct:.4f}% and €100M requires {required_probability_100_pct:.4f}%. These are neither forecasts nor inferred from small benchmarks. A €3M priced round at €50M pre-money gives {new_investor_pct:.4f}% initial investor ownership before option-pool changes, fees, preferences or future rounds; at €100M it gives {stretch_new_investor_pct:.4f}%. An investor must independently accept technology scalability, commercial value capture, rights and execution to support a premium price.
slides.banner: Required odds are reverse-calculated conditions. The benchmarks do not estimate those probabilities.

slides.title: The price depends on dilution, exit scale and time.

At a €3B outcome and 10% retained equity, the required probabilities are much higher than at a €30B exit with 50% retention. A lower discount rate increases the present value, while delays and dilution reduce it. In the €3M/€50M round, an investor retains 1.6981% at exit if 30% of its initial stake survives, giving €{conditional_proceeds_m_eur:.2f}M or {conditional_moic:.2f}× gross MOIC in the assumed €10B success outcome. That conditional upside is not expected return; failure is zero and cash-flow timing/preferences are omitted.
